question.text: Among the following, the incorrect statement about colloids is:

options.text: They are larger than small molecules and have high molar mass.
The osmotic pressure of a collodial solution is of higher order than the true solution at the same concentration.

The range of diameters of colloidal particles is between <math><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mn>1000</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text: Due to the bigger size of colloidal particles the number of particles in a colloidal solution is comparatively small as compared to a true solution. Hence the values of colligative properties are of small order as compared to values shown by true solutions at same concentration.
